reason: The cited select case waits for a selector and calls page.select(args.selector, args.value), then returns only a confirmation string based on the supplied arguments. It does not return page contents or other non-public data, and it does not return attacker-controlled web content. The lines do show Puppeteer launching a browser, but they do not by themselves establish arbitrary host code execution; launch options/source of mergedConfig are not shown. Similarly, selecting a value may interact with whatever page is open, but these lines alone do not establish delivery to an attacker-readable destination.
